X.note: The photo is shown as a tilted print on a vignetted dark-brown backdrop, which gives some depth. The lower-third text is clean, with a gold accent bar, and clearly names the person, role and date. The photo credit box slightly overlaps the print's lower-left corner. The right side is a bit empty, and the print is small in the frame, so the face is tiny on a phone.

Y.note: This is a full-bleed streetscape that looks atmospheric, with a bottom gradient behind the text. The caption 'judges deferred to local lawmakers' has no visible link to the image. The photo shows an empty tree-lined street and a mansion. The source line is small, low-contrast grey and sits over a busy part of the photo. It reads as a plain stock-photo-plus-caption layout with no depth or motion cues.

why: X frames the photograph as a physical object and labels it clearly, so a viewer knows who and when at a glance, while Y is a generic street photo with a caption that doesn't match what is shown and a small, low-contrast source line.
top_fix_for_weaker: Add a purposeful focal element, such as a slow push-in or highlight on the mansion with a short label like 'Local zoning power', then enlarge the source line and give it a solid or darker backing strip. Also tie the caption to the image, or replace the image with one that depicts judges or lawmakers.
